findings.evidence: “Clear: Content is immediately understandable” and the subsequent whitespace, consistency, and concise-bullet guidance largely repeat presentation knowledge the model already has. The main Quality check section also primarily provides activation rather than new expertise.
findings.fix: Trim the generic presentation tutorial. Retain the bundled-style decisions, Marpit-specific layout behavior, export limitations, and concrete rendering failures that the agent would otherwise miss.

findings.evidence: “Start from assets/template-*.md” is the single authoring procedure, although the description also promises improvements to existing decks. There is no redesign-specific checkpoint for preserving existing content, notes, branding, or working layouts.
findings.fix: Branch the workflow into new-deck creation and existing-deck redesign. For redesign, inspect the current deck, identify what must be preserved, diagnose its rendered problems, and apply only the necessary template or CSS changes.

findings.evidence: “Concise: About 15-25 characters per line” imposes a language-insensitive text limit on creative slide content, despite the main workflow correctly prioritizing rendered readability.
findings.fix: Replace the character limit with a rendered-fit principle: preserve complete claims, avoid distracting wrapping, and split content when the chosen font and layout become difficult to read.

findings.evidence: “Has lead title styling and embedded styling from the selected template” checks source structure, but the three evals do not exercise existing-deck redesign, image resolution, or the gradient variants whose rendered quality the workflow explicitly requires checking.
findings.fix: Add an existing-deck fixture and a multi-variant gradient/image case. Assert preserved requested content, resolved assets, readable contrast, absence of overflow, and truthful reporting when rendering is unavailable.

findings.evidence: “background: linear-gradient(135deg, #4facfe 0%, #00f2fe 100%)” is paired with white body text. Following the gradient-style branch produces a bright cyan variant with inadequate text contrast; the external gradient stylesheet repeats this combination.
findings.fix: Darken the bright gradient stops or place text on a sufficiently opaque dark surface. Apply the correction to both gradient assets and verify every variant, not only the title slide.

findings.evidence: The supplied GitHub Actions build uses “actions/upload-artifact@v3”, a retired action version that prevents the documented workflow from completing on GitHub.com.
findings.fix: Update the artifact upload to a supported version such as actions/upload-artifact@v4, update the checkout action as appropriate, and verify that the example successfully uploads the generated PDF.
